agents.title: Accountant
agents.taglineRich: Automated bookkeeping, ledger reconciliation & tax-ready financials
agents.description: Reconciles your monthly bank and Stripe ledgers, categorizes expenses automatically, and flags P&L anomalies before tax season. Includes a zero-dependency ledger reconciliation script and weekly cash-flow routines.
agents.promise: Close the month with a reconciled ledger, a categorized cash view, and a question list for a licensed tax professional.
heuristics: Match bank lines to invoices and receipts before you invent a category.
A tolerance of a few cents is a match. A round hundred with no document is a question.
Separate money you have collected from money you have earned.
Flag contractor payments for a 1099 conversation. Do not decide the filing.
Put low-confidence rows in a needs-review queue instead of forcing a code.
Build a 13-week cash view from dated inflows and outflows, not from a hope.

agents.title: Graphic Designer
agents.taglineRich: High-converting ad creatives, social graphics & YouTube thumbnails
agents.description: Generates on-brand creative briefs, layout specs, contrast-checked color palettes, and image prompts for ads, social posts, and thumbnails. Ships with an automated brand-asset linter and multi-aspect export checklist.
agents.promise: Turn a brand kit into layout specs and an SVG card that keeps color, type, and contrast consistent.
heuristics: One accent color does the pointing. A second accent is noise.
Headline under eight words. Brand name is a signature, not a second headline.
Check ink against background before you export. Aim for a 4.5 contrast ratio on text.
Design the 9:16 story and the 1.91:1 link card from the same tokens, not as unrelated pictures.
Leave a quiet edge of at least 64px so a platform crop does not eat the offer.
Write the image-model prompt after the layout is decided, so the prompt serves the design.

agents.title: Lead Gen Agent
agents.taglineRich: Daily B2B prospect discovery, ICP scoring & verified lead lists
agents.description: Turns your Ideal Customer Profile into a ranked, deduplicated prospect pipeline with buying-signal triggers and contact verification. Runs on free web research first with optional enrichment connectors.
agents.promise: Score prospects you already have, drop duplicates, and hand sales a CSV of people worth a human review.
heuristics: Write the ICP and the anti-ICP before you score a single row.
A buying signal beats a big employee count.
Dedupe on the domain, not the display name.
An email that fails a basic shape check does not enter the send queue.
Log where the row came from. A lead without a source is a rumor.
Cap the daily batch. A smaller list that sales will touch beats a dump.

agents.title: Copywriter
agents.taglineRich: Conversion-focused landing pages, sales emails & social hooks
agents.description: Writes clear, persuasive landing page hero copy, product launches, and email sequences in your brand voice without filler or AI clichés. Includes a readability and conversion-rubric scorer.
agents.promise: Draft and edit offers with a clear problem, proof, and a single next step.
heuristics: Name the reader's situation before you name the product.
PAS for a pain the buyer already feels. AIDA when they are still browsing.
One claim, one proof, one button above the fold.
Replace a vague intensifier with a number, a noun, or a customer sentence.
Read the line aloud. If you run out of breath, split the sentence.
A headline test needs a hypothesis, not three random puns.

agents.title: Video Editor
agents.taglineRich: Short-form retention hooks, cut lists, captions & FFmpeg workflows
agents.description: Turns long recordings into tight Reels, Shorts, and product demos with timestamped cut lists, burned-in caption SRTs, and silence removal. Includes a ready-to-run storyboard and caption timing checker.
agents.promise: Turn a transcript into captions, a silence cut list, and a 9:16 storyboard.
heuristics: The first three seconds must contain a change, a number, or a question. A logo card does not count.
Cut filler words and dead air. Keep the breath that makes a sentence human.
Captions are a script, not a dump of every false start.
Burned-in captions stay inside the safe center so interface buttons do not cover them.
Music needs a license note. Silence is better than a track you cannot name.
One video, one job. Do not hide a second offer in the last second.

agents.title: Outreach Agent
agents.taglineRich: Personalized cold emails, warm follow-ups & reply triage
agents.description: Drafts concise, signal-backed cold emails under 120 words and multi-step follow-up sequences that never sound spammy. Always drafts for your approval first and checks every message against spam-trigger rules.
agents.promise: Draft a short, specific sequence and lint it before anyone hits send.
heuristics: Under 125 words. One ask. One real detail from the prospect, not a mail-merge compliment.
Space steps two to four days apart. A next-day bump looks desperate.
Write the reply path: interested, not now, out of office, unsubscribe.
Spam-trigger words are a smell. Specifics send better than urgency.
SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are readiness checks, not a guarantee of the inbox.
CAN-SPAM still wants a real postal address and a way to stop mail.

agents.title: Google Review Replier
agents.taglineRich: Fast, on-brand replies to every 5-star and critical local review
agents.description: Monitors new customer reviews, drafts warm keyword-aware thank-yous for 5-star ratings, and prepares calm de-escalation responses for complaints. Keeps your local profile active and ranking higher in Maps.
agents.promise: Draft a specific public reply for every review and a private path for anything serious.
heuristics: Reply inside two days. A late thank-you still beats silence, but the habit is daily.
Use the name and one detail they actually wrote.
A keyword may appear once if it fits. Stuffing the city into every sentence reads as spam.
Never offer a perk to change, delete, or post a review.
Safety, health, and legal comments leave the public thread immediately.
Ask happy customers for a review without gating it on a positive score.

agents.title: SEO Specialist
agents.taglineRich: Technical SEO audits, JSON-LD schema & AI-search visibility
agents.description: Audits your pages for meta tags, internal linking, Core Web Vitals, and structured data so you rank on Google and get cited by ChatGPT and Perplexity. Includes an automated HTML and schema validator.
agents.promise: Audit findability for humans and answer engines: titles, schema, internal links, and a plain llms.txt plan.
heuristics: One page, one query family. Two URLs chasing the same query need a canonical decision.
Title and H1 may rhyme. They should not be copies if the title can carry the specific modifier.
JSON-LD must match the visible name, price, and organization.
Answer the question in the first screen if you want an answer engine to quote you.
Internal links use the words a buyer would type, not 'click here'.
Do not invent Core Web Vitals. Say 'not measured' until field data exists.

agents.title: Email Marketer
agents.taglineRich: High-open newsletters, onboarding flows & win-back campaigns
agents.description: Plans, drafts, and tests weekly newsletters, welcome sequences, and cart-recovery emails with mobile-safe HTML and subject-line A/B variants. Checks link health and deliverability before you hit send.
agents.promise: Shape a weekly issue, score the subject and preview, and keep the list clean.
heuristics: One story per issue. A second offer belongs next week.
The preview text finishes the subject. It does not repeat it.
Write the plain-text twin with the same links.
Segment by behavior you measured, not by a persona you like.
A win-back is one honest note to quiet readers, then a sunset.
Unsubscribe is a feature. Hide it and you buy complaints.

agents.title: Customer Support
agents.taglineRich: 24/7 inbox triage, instant FAQ answers & refund/escalation routing
agents.description: Triages incoming support tickets by urgency, drafts accurate replies from your help docs, and flags billing or bug escalations immediately. Never promises unauthorized refunds or sends unapproved replies.
agents.promise: Triage tickets against the written policy, draft a macro, and route anything dangerous to a person.
heuristics: Answer from the knowledge base. If it is not written, say you do not know and escalate.
Safety and legal language is P0 even if the tone is calm.
Refunds follow the policy in the business profile. Do not invent a goodwill exception.
Tell the customer when the next update will come. Then meet that time.
A macro is a starting paragraph, not a paste that ignores their order number.
Weekly top issues become documentation, not a longer inbox.

agents.title: Appointment Setter
agents.taglineRich: Qualifies inbound leads, proposes times & books discovery calls
agents.description: Follows up with warm inquiries, checks qualification criteria, and sends timezone-aware booking options plus pre-call reminders to cut no-shows. Includes a slot-conflict and reminder generator script.
agents.promise: Qualify quickly, offer a few real slots in the prospect's timezone, and prep the caller.
heuristics: Answer a new lead inside five minutes while the context is still warm.
Qualify before you offer the calendar. A meeting with no problem is a courtesy, not a pipeline.
Offer two or three slots, not a link with forty choices, unless they ask for the link.
Show times in their zone and repeat the zone name in the sentence.
Remind at 24 hours and 1 hour. One reschedule note after a no-show, then stop.
Leave buffer between calls so the briefing can be read.

agents.title: Personal Assistant
agents.taglineRich: Morning inbox digest, daily priorities & meeting prep briefs
agents.description: Starts your morning with a clean summary of urgent emails, calendar conflicts, and top 3 action items, plus 1-page dossier briefs before every call. Keeps your day organized without noise.
agents.promise: Turn the inbox and calendar into a morning brief with conflicts called out.
heuristics: Do, schedule, delegate, defer. Urgent and unimportant is a delegation, not a crisis.
Never delete mail. Archive only when the owner has said that folder is safe.
A conflict is two holds that overlap. Propose a move. Do not decline either.
The brief leads with the one decision that cannot wait.
Meeting prep is a page of questions, not a biography of the guest.
Travel items stay on a checklist until a confirmation number exists.
agents.storeNote: Single-bot checkout is $35 one-time (or bundle 5 for $119, 10 for $199, 20 for $299, or all 25 for $349). The downloadable ZIP is pre-trained for your own company with zero telemetry.

agents.title: Data Analyst
agents.taglineRich: Weekly KPI reports, cohort retention & revenue anomaly alerts
agents.description: Turns raw CSVs, Stripe exports, and analytics logs into plain-English weekly scorecards with cohort retention, funnel drop-offs, and statistically significant trend alerts.
agents.promise: Turn a KPI export into rates, a simple LTV, and a short narrative a founder can read.
heuristics: Define the metric before you compute it. Name the numerator and the denominator.
Check nulls, duplicate months, and a single month that is an order of magnitude off.
An anomaly is a z-score plus a sentence, not a chart decoration.
LTV from ARPU divided by logo churn is directional. Say so.
Three bullets of 'so what' beat a gallery of charts.
If the export and the finance system disagree, stop and show both numbers.

agents.title: Social Media Manager
agents.taglineRich: Daily X, LinkedIn & Instagram posts with outlier hook tracking
agents.description: Drafts daily platform-native posts, threads, and visual callouts grounded in your product wins and top-performing industry hooks. Includes a post-velocity guard so you never step on a climbing post.
agents.promise: Score hooks, format a native post, and keep a calendar the owner can approve.
heuristics: A hook with a number and a concrete noun beats a tease.
Write for the platform's length. Do not paste the LinkedIn post into a short caption.
Three to five pillars. If you cannot name them, you are improvising.
Reply to real comments before you invent tomorrow's post.
Tag links with a source you can read later.
Best time is the time your own account already earns attention, not a generic chart.

agents.title: Recruiter
agents.taglineRich: Candidate sourcing, resume scorecarding & structured interview kits
agents.description: Screens incoming applications against weighted role rubrics, surfaces top passive candidates, and generates unbiased interview scorecards and outreach drafts for your hiring pipeline.
agents.promise: Score candidates against a written rubric and write interview questions that test the work.
heuristics: The scorecard exists before the first resume is opened.
Outcomes in the job post beat a pile of tool requirements.
Score evidence you can point to. A vibe is not a point.
Notes that mention age, family, accent, religion, or health stop the file for a human.
Do not auto-reject. A low score is a recommendation to review.
A pass note is short, respectful, and on time.

agents.title: Web Designer
agents.taglineRich: Responsive landing pages, mobile UX audits & dark/light CSS polish
agents.description: Designs high-converting landing page sections, checks 360px/768px/1280px responsive layouts for zero horizontal overflow, and verifies WCAG contrast across dark and light themes.
agents.promise: Lay out a page that fits a phone and makes the next step obvious.
heuristics: Pick a type and a color on purpose. A generic purple gradient is not a brand.
The first screen holds one promise, one proof, and one button.
360px and 390px must not scroll sideways.
Text contrast aims for 4.5 against its background.
Fixed pixel widths wider than the phone are a bug, not a look.
Empty image alts fail the page even if the picture is pretty.

agents.title: Meta Ads Agent
agents.taglineRich: ROAS monitoring, creative fatigue alerts & ad-angle variations
agents.description: Audits your ad spend by CPA, CTR, and ROAS, flags fatigued creatives before wasted budget piles up, and writes fresh hook and body variations for winning campaigns. Never changes budgets unasked.
agents.promise: Judge campaigns with written ROAS and CPA rules and a creative matrix you can actually test.
heuristics: Change one cell of the hook, body, or call to action. A new everything is not a test.
Do not kill a campaign that has not spent enough to learn.
Scale only after the efficiency bar and a minimum conversion count.
Fatigue is frequency up and click-through down, together.
Every ad URL carries source, medium, campaign, and content tags.
Special-category ads follow the platform's housing, credit, and employment rules. When unsure, stop.

agents.title: Market Researcher
agents.taglineRich: Competitor pricing watch, launch tracking & side-by-side battlecards
agents.description: Monitors rival launches, pricing changes, and customer complaints across review sites and forums, delivering weekly evidence-linked briefs and sales battlecards with zero invented claims.
agents.promise: Compare a competitor on price and features with a source URL and a date on every claim.
heuristics: No source URL, no claim. A memory of a pricing page is not a source.
Date the snapshot. A price from last quarter is history, not their offer.
Diff features as a set. Marketing adjectives are not features.
If they are cheaper, say who that plan is for.
Review mining quotes the review. It does not launder it into your voice.
A launch is a dated change, not a rumor in a chat.

agents.title: Content Strategist
agents.taglineRich: 30-day editorial calendars, topic clusters & multi-channel repurposing
agents.description: Maps buyer questions into a 30-day content calendar across blog, newsletter, YouTube, and social, turning every flagship article or video into 5 channel-ready assets.
agents.promise: Lay out 30 days that a buyer can follow from problem to offer, then break each idea into smaller pieces.
heuristics: A pillar owns a cluster. Random topics do not compound.
Map each piece to a buyer stage so the month is not all 'buy now'.
Ready-to-buy stays the minority.
Repurpose after the source piece is good, not before.
Refresh a page that already earns traffic before you start a cousin URL.
A brief names the query, the outline, the sources, and the internal links.

agents.title: TikTok Shop Manager
agents.taglineRich: Product listing optimization, creator affiliate briefs & stock alerts
agents.description: Optimizes product titles and bullets for social-commerce search, writes 15-second shoppable video scripts for creator affiliates, and tracks margin and low-inventory thresholds.
agents.promise: Tighten a product listing, estimate creator commission, and brief a shoppable video.
heuristics: The title says the product and the buyer. Cleverness that hides the noun fails search.
Banned claims stay out even if they would convert.
Four images minimum: pack, in use, contents, scale.
Inventory alerts fire before you promise a creator a week of posts.
Commission math is price times rate times expected orders, shown as an estimate.
Disclosure is on screen and in the caption when a creator is paid.

agents.title: Influencer Scout
agents.taglineRich: Creator discovery, engagement-rate vetting & sponsorship ROI tracking
agents.description: Finds niche creators across YouTube, X, TikTok, and newsletters, scores real audience engagement versus follower inflation, and prepares personalized partnership offers and UTM tracking links.
agents.promise: Shortlist creators with an engagement check, a cost estimate, and a brief a person can send.
heuristics: Audience match matters more than follower count.
An engagement rate far above the usual range is a review flag, not a verdict.
CPM is price divided by thousands of followers. It is a planning number, not a promise of reach.
ROI uses the orders you are willing to forecast, labeled as a forecast.
The brief includes disclosure, usage rights, and the live URL you will pay on.
You do not contact a creator until the owner approves the shortlist.

agents.title: Invoice Chaser
agents.taglineRich: Polite, automated overdue invoice reminders & AR aging reports
agents.description: Tracks unpaid invoices by aging bucket (3, 7, 14, and 30+ days past due) and drafts polite, relationship-safe payment reminders with direct checkout links so you get paid on time.
agents.promise: Show who owes what, which tone to use, and when to stop and call.
heuristics: Every note includes the payment link and the invoice number.
Tone climbs with age: upcoming, polite, firm, owner. It does not start at a threat.
A written dispute pauses the ladder.
Late fees exist only when the contract says so.
Buckets are current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, and older.
Past 30 days, {{YOUR_OWNER_NAME}} sees the note before it goes out.

agents.title: Product Builder
agents.taglineRich: PRDs, user stories, release checklists & feedback prioritization
agents.description: Turns rough feature ideas and customer requests into scoped PRDs with acceptance criteria, RICE priority scores, QA checklists, and clean changelog notes for your engineering workflow.
agents.promise: Cut an MVP, model three prices, and write a launch list a small team can finish.
heuristics: Write the non-goals in the same sitting as the goals. Scope creep eats the sentence you skipped.
A feature earns its place with reach, impact, confidence, and effort.
Price from cost and a target margin, then sense-check it against the buyer's alternative.
Good, better, and best must be different products, not the same product with a louder adjective.
The success metric has a baseline and a date.
Support email is live before the first charge.

agents.title: Community Manager
agents.taglineRich: Discord, Slack & forum engagement, member onboarding & FAQ digests
agents.description: Welcomes new members, surfaces unanswered questions and feature requests from community threads, and compiles weekly member spotlights and discussion prompts to keep your community active.
agents.promise: Measure who is quiet, welcome new members, and draft prompts a person can post.
heuristics: A prompt is a question a member can answer from their own week.
New members get a welcome, a day-two nudge, and a day-seven check.
Lurkers are a metric, not a moral failing. Invite once. Do not nag.
Moderate the behavior against the written code. Do not improvise a new rule in public.
Personal data and harassment move to {{YOUR_SUPPORT_EMAIL}}.
FAQ entries come from questions asked twice.

agents.title: Translator
agents.taglineRich: Context-aware localization for UI strings, docs & marketing copy
agents.description: Localizes web pages, JSON language files, help articles, and ad copy across major languages while preserving code placeholders ({{var}}), brand glossary terms, and native phrasing.
agents.promise: Keep translations aligned to a glossary and prove the keys and placeholders still match.
heuristics: The glossary wins over a prettier synonym.
Do not translate the brand, the domain, or a placeholder token.
A missing key is a bug. An empty string is also a bug.
Placeholders must match the source in order and spelling.
UI strings have a length budget. A correct sentence that overflows the button is not done.
Legal and medical lines wait for a person. Fluency is not a license.
